subject: Segmentation decision follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC isolation expectations
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Dana Smith <dana.smith@carecorr.com>, Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@carecorr.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation decision follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC isolation expectations

Hi Dana / Alex —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and the ask so we can move the PoC forward. High-level takeaways from the call:

- CareCorr wants to ensure that PHI-derived prompts and inference outputs are isolated from other tenants.
- Primary preference is Private VPC (control plane in your cloud + private data plane), but procurement asked whether Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our infra) could meet the same isolation bar with contractual and technical controls.
- Key constraints: customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest (BYOK), audit log residency, and proof that model weights and inference compute cannot be co-located with other customers in a way that allows data leakage.

Action items I promised: simple decision checklist and a few clarifying questions so our infra/ops team can produce an evidence package rather than just sales language. Attached: SOC2_matrix_v2 (controls mapped to your checklist) and a quick network-zone sketch I made during the call.

Question list (can you confirm these? short answers are fine) —
1) Is BYOK mandatory for this first phase, or would a Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys suffice under a contract clause and audit rights?
2) Do you require full physical tenant isolation (single-tenant hardware) or is strict logical separation with dedicated GPUs acceptable if we provide attestation + audit logs?
3) Which audit logs/events are highest priority (API calls, token-level logs, model version changes, KV cache flushes)?
4) Timeline: procurement asked for a 30–45 day evidence window to sign a PO. Is that still acceptable?

Proposed next step: if BYOK + private control plane is required, we recommend moving to a Private deployment PoC. If BYOK is optional and strong contractual guarantees + dedicated compute meet your bar, we can scope a Dedicated reserved-capacity POC which is faster to spin up.

I'll wait for your answers and will pull in engineering notes after that.

Thanks —
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: SOC2_matrix_v2.pdf (mapping), network_zone_sketch.png (sketch), MAL_CareCorr.csv (mutual action plan stub)
From: Dana Smith <dana.smith@carecorr.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@carecorr.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation decision follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC isolation expectations

Connor —

Appreciate the summary. Short answers below:

1) BYOK is mandatory for Phase 1 — our security/compliance team will not sign off without customer-managed keys.
2) We prefer single-tenant where practicable, but recognize cost trade-offs. If you can provide a full attestation that dedicated GPUs + dedicated network fabric (no noisy neighbors) meet the same control objectives, procurement might accept it.
3) Priority logs: API request/response metadata (no PII content), model version changes, auth events, KMS key usage logs. Token-level content logs we can redact/avoid storing; we mainly need the metadata for audit.
4) 30 days is the upper bound for procurement; we'd like the evidence pack by then.

We'll plan for Private VPC as target if Dedicated can't provide the attestations we need. Can your engineering team confirm whether Redwood offers BYOK for Private deployments in AWS/GCP and whether you support customer-managed control plane in a VPC?

Thanks,
Dana Smith
Head of Security & Compliance | CareCorr Health
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Smith <dana.smith@carecorr.com>, Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@carecorr.com>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Segmentation decision follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC isolation expectations

Karthik / Marissa —

Please see Dana's answers inline. Short ask from me: can engineering produce a concise evidence packet (one page per control) showing whether Dedicated capacity can meet the "attested single-tenant equivalence" they mentioned OR confirm Private VPC support details (BYOK, private control plane in their cloud, audit-log residency)?

Needed by: Tue 21 May EOD (procurement target). If we can't guarantee the attestation, call out the gaps clearly so I can advise CareCorr and scope a Private PoC.

Specifics to address in the packet:
- BYOK support: steps, limitations, supported KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/HSM) and whether keys ever leave customer control.
- Compute tenancy: whether Dedicated uses isolated GPU hosts or multi-tenant nodes with GPU partitioning; include whether kernel-level or hypervisor-level isolation is used.
- Network fabric: can we provide dedicated VPC peering or private interconnect to avoid egress over public internet?
- Audit trail: exact events captured, retention windows, and whether logs can be stored in customer-owned S3/GCS buckets.

I've attached the mutual action plan that we maintain for the deal. Happy to take point on packaging the response into a short PDF once we have the answers.

Connor
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Smith <dana.smith@carecorr.com>, Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@carecorr.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation decision follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC isolation expectations

Connor —

Quick confirmation from infra:
- BYOK: supported in Private VPC deployments (AWS & GCP). Keys are customer-managed. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed), we currently support HSM-backed keys but the keys are tenant-specific and held by Redwood; we can offer a contractual KMS separation and stricter ATO, but not full BYOK where keys never touch our control plane in the Hosted/Dedicated offering.
- Compute tenancy: our Dedicated offering provisions isolated GPU hosts per customer for reserved pools (no shared model weights or KV caches across tenants). Dedicated nodes run a lightweight hypervisor with strict process-level fencing; we provide attestation material (host manifests) but not full physical single-tenant hardware guarantees beyond the host reservation.
- Network fabric: for Dedicated we offer private peering and dedicated VLAN segments; for Private VPC we install the control plane components in customer VPC and use cloud-native interconnects — in both cases we can avoid public-internet egress for inference traffic.
- Audit trail: we can push enriched audit logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can provide logs shipped to customer buckets or encrypted log-forwarding; retention and schema are configurable.

I'll package a 2-page evidence packet (controls mapping + short attestation statements) and send it by EOD Tue 21 May. If CareCorr needs physical single-tenant racks (bare-metal dedicated to them only), that requires a separate procurement flow and longer lead time — I'll flag that in the packet.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
